profile.headline: Software Engineer
profile.shortBio: I’m ambitious, relentlessly curious, and always looking for the next hard problem to learn from. I care about moving with urgency, doing things well, and getting better with every project.
profile.longBio: I build practical software systems at the intersection of full-stack engineering, AI/ML, computer vision, and security. My work includes research software for microscopy analysis, adversarial machine learning pipelines, teaching support for core CS courses, and production-style projects using Next.js, Flask, Django, Firebase, and cloud deployment tooling.
profile.experienceSummary: My experience spans AI engineering at the U.S. Treasury, research software and machine learning at the University of Washington, and teaching core computer science courses.

research.title: CytoCV: Reproducible Yeast Microscopy Analysis
research.organizationLogoAlt: UW Bothell School of STEM logo
research.homeSummary: Open-source Django platform that uses DIC-guided Mask R-CNN segmentation to turn DeltaVision and TIFF yeast microscopy stacks into reviewable per-cell fluorescence measurements and structured exports.
profileLabs: SEE Lab, UW Bothell School of STEM
research.detailSummary: Architected microscopy ingestion, DIC-guided Mask R-CNN inference, worker-backed analysis, PostgreSQL persistence, and production Linux delivery.
research.impact: Released CytoCV v2.0.0 as a citable open-source software artifact with a versioned DOI.
bullets: Translated biology-facing requirements into channel-aware DeltaVision and TIFF ingestion
Engineered cell and cell-pair segmentation with reviewable multichannel overlays
Built configurable puncta distance, biorientation, contour intensity, and nuclear analysis workflows
Designed background jobs, progress and cancellation flows, protected artifacts, and durable result storage
Led production deployment, regression testing, documentation, and ongoing maintenance
research.graphicalAbstractAlt: Four-step CytoCV workflow from yeast microscopy channels through segmentation and fluorescence measurement to reviewable CSV/XLSX export.

research.title: Adversarial Machine Learning
research.organizationLogoAlt: UW Bothell School of STEM logo
research.homeSummary: Independent study that prototyped four adversarial attack families and four defensive strategies with ART and TensorFlow/Keras across standard image-classification benchmarks.
research.detailSummary: Integrated ART primitives with TensorFlow/Keras models to test evasion, extraction, inversion, poisoning, detection, preprocessing, postprocessing, and distillation workflows.
research.impact: Built eight focused attack-and-defense prototypes across MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10.
bullets: Generated DeepFool adversarial examples and built Copycat CNN extraction experiments
Built MIFace model-inversion and corner-trigger backdoor-poisoning experiments
Trained an adversarial-input detector on FGM samples and evaluated JPEG preprocessing
Compared Gaussian-noise postprocessing and defensive distillation
Measured attack success and clean, attacked, and defended model accuracy
research.graphicalAbstractAlt: Four-step adversarial machine-learning study showing image-classification data and models, attack experiments, defense experiments, and evaluation outputs.

research.title: Guide Donor Scheduler: Yeast CRISPR Sequence Design
research.organizationLogoAlt: UW Bothell School of STEM logo
research.homeSummary: Python pipeline that converts yeast FASTA sequences and requested amino-acid substitutions into CRISPR/Cas9 guide and donor constructs with strand-aware PAM handling and researcher-ready XLS output.
research.detailSummary: Built a configurable Python CLI with FASTA ingestion, strand-aware PAM discovery, codon-aware mutation rules, ranked candidate selection, and XLS generation.
research.impact: Automated guide and donor design from sequence input to traceable, order-ready results.
bullets: Located forward NGG and reverse-strand CCN PAM sites across FASTA records
Encoded amino-acid substitutions with codon-aware silent PAM and seed edits
Supported guide filtering, ranking, duplicate removal, validation, kill guides, and reverse complements
Generated color-coded XLS workbooks with guides, PAMs, mutation offsets, cut-site distances, and decision rationale
Tested inversion, PAM discovery, mutation generation, disruption, and adjacent mutations in GitHub Actions
research.graphicalAbstractAlt: Four-step GuideDonorScheduler workflow from FASTA input through guide selection and donor design to annotated XLS output.

projects.title: Clair
projects.subtitle: Customizable desktop file organizer
projects.homeSummary: Sorts files into folders by type with customizable categories, reusable presets, recursive scanning, and optional empty-folder cleanup.

homeSkills.name: Python
homeSkills.details: Python 3.11 and the standard os module scan selected folders, map file extensions to JSON-defined categories, create destination folders, move files, and optionally remove empty directories.

homeSkills.name: Bash
homeSkills.summary: Bash supports Clair's source-based development workflow.
homeSkills.details: Shell commands create and activate the development environment, install Python requirements, and launch the application from source; Clair's sorting logic itself remains Python-based.

homeSkills.name: PySide6
homeSkills.summary: PySide6 provides Clair's cross-platform desktop interface.
homeSkills.details: Qt for Python renders the dark-mode controls for folder selection, category and extension management, reusable presets, recursive scanning, optional cleanup, and the one-click organization workflow.

projects.detailSummary: A cross-platform desktop utility for organizing folders through a polished Qt interface and user-defined file rules.
projects.problem: Downloads and working folders quickly become difficult to navigate when files use inconsistent naming and locations.
projects.solution: Maps extensions to editable categories, applies reusable presets, and packages the workflow as a standalone desktop application.

projects.title: LeetNotes
projects.subtitle: Automated LeetCode study system
projects.homeSummary: Keeps Google Sheets study data synchronized with structured notes, generated Python solutions, indexed problem folders, and scheduled repository updates.

homeSkills.name: Python
homeSkills.summary: Python implements the LeetNotes synchronization CLI.
homeSkills.details: The package reads published sheet CSVs, normalizes problem titles and LeetCode slugs, generates Markdown study notes, writes solution.py variants, and maintains the repository's indexed problem structure.

homeSkills.name: GitHub Actions
homeSkills.summary: GitHub Actions keeps generated study material synchronized.
homeSkills.details: The scheduled notes.yml workflow runs the CLI, rebuilds notes and solution files from published sheet data, and commits any repository changes for review.

homeSkills.name: Google Sheets
homeSkills.summary: Google Sheets serves as LeetNotes' editable content source.
homeSkills.details: Each list uses paired Notes and Solutions sheets published as CSV: one stores problem metadata, approaches, complexity, and study notes; the other stores plain-text Python solutions.

projects.detailSummary: A Python CLI and scheduled automation workflow that turns spreadsheet-authored problem notes and solutions into a consistent interview-preparation repository.
projects.problem: Daily problem-solving notes and solution files become difficult to keep consistent across spreadsheets and folders.
projects.solution: Normalizes problem metadata, generates Markdown and Python files, and uses GitHub Actions to keep the repository synchronized on a schedule.

recommendations.fullQuote: Nicolas has worked with me on an open source project, CytoCV, in collaboration with biologists at the University of Utah. He has excelled in many critical areas on this project including software engineering, web development, UX, computer vision, and the ability to work with biologists and translate their needs into software. Nicolas is proactive in identifying and solving issues and has demonstrated excellent skills in writing, documentation, and collaboration.

I highly recommend Nicolas for software engineering and development roles. I was his instructor for two undergraduate CSS courses and then he was a grader for two CSS courses. Nicolas is dedicated, detail-oriented, and has strong collaboration skills. I counted on him to provide meaningful feedback on student work, and he was proactive in raising issues and potential solutions. He will be a great asset to his future teams!

recommendations.relationship: Worked with Nicolas on the same team
recommendations.fullQuote: Since January 2026, I have had the pleasure of working with Nicolas on the CytoCV platform, improving both functionality and usability throughout the application. Not only was his work prior to my having joined the project in September 2025 a solid foundation, but in my time working with him directly, he has been a reliable, hard worker with strong technical and problem solving skills, as well as extremely professional. He is a strong communicator, including across disciplines, and highly organized, maintaining the documentation of CytoCV's GitHub repository expertly. He has produced consistently high-quality work, and has been invaluable to the project; any team would benefit from his work ethic, positive attitude, and skills.

recommendations.relationship: Worked with Nicolas on the same team
recommendations.fullQuote: I collaborated with Nick on several university engineering projects, where he proved to be a reliable and versatile developer. He managed our full-stack workflow seamlessly including structuring backend logic with Python, Django, and SQL, while keeping our frontends functional with JavaScript, HTML5, and CSS. He has solid engineering discipline, working comfortably across Linux environments, Git version control, and Azure cloud deployment.
